x: Although my subjects are a little older than this, and you may need to watch for rather more than one season, I would commend to my favoured clients the following promising specimens:-John Dear. Peter Hilliar,Dick Calderwood, Ron Sinclair, Doug Brew, Bob James and Joe Riley.

Chris Steer's effort was particularly good - he improves every time out. D.Brew and R.James indicated we shall be seeing quite a lot more of them - the latter winning the handicap jointly with Adrian Major.

David Davies ran a well deserved 2nd place whilst another face to reappear after a long absence from the athletic scene was Bob James in 3rd spot---some shady training in the Coulsdon area indicated here; no doubt catching the habit from near neighbour Clive Shippen!!.
The late arrival of Alan Black and Charlie Walker prevented their getting more favourable runs in the B team, whilst Bob James showed a fine return to fitness after being inactive for so long.

Having won the race last year our successful scoring team joined the many other Belgravians who are barred from this event. We were therefore very weakly represented, though Colin Pearson and Bob James showed promising form.

We might have expected John Kelly to head our challenge, but John had come on from ammorning run over 2,000m. as part of the Lord Mayor's Show, and finished back in 123rd place - Bob James' 72nd taking the honours.

It could be, at the same time, that Guy Monnet will produce an even more considerable breakthrough in coming weeks than he has already this winter, while Colin Pearson, John Kelly and Bob James are all threatening to break out of the second team ranks into the first team before long.
